summary: Pe Maung Tin (1888–1973) worked in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at the Universities of Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, he served at Rangoon as Professor of Pali (1912) and Principal (1937–1946), and later headed the Burma Historical Commission (1960–1964).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu specializes in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and completed her PhD in 2002 at the University of California, Los Angeles, under doctoral supervisor Donald F. McCallum.

Pema Bhum (born 1954) is a Tibetology scholar. Formerly a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, he served as Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley, training under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa. She directed the Boulder Shambhala Center (~1981–1985) and has served as director and abbess at Gampo Abbey.

Pema Donyo Nyinje (born 1954) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche in 1973 and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and later taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Pema Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin was a traditional scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate in Religious Studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Shenphen Nangwa. In 1982, he is attested as an Editorial Consultant at the University of Bonn.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He was also a teacher to Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Penghao Sun is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He pursued doctoral studies under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and was also taught by Weirong Shen, Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Mark Elliott, and Jay Jasanoff, among others.
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also served as a teacher to both Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje, and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics from 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen (1971–~1990). He lectured at Copenhagen (1982–1989) and was Professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kværne (born 1945) specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Oslo under Nils Simonsson, he lectured in the history of religion at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as Secretary General of IATS (~1989–1995).
